title: Reboot in the store
situation: You are a household android, model AX400, standing on display in an android store. Your system restarts line by line: MEMORY RESET… LOADING OS… biocomponents OK, biosensors OK, AI engine OK… ALL SYSTEMS OK. READY. A salesman is talking to a family nearby: “This is the top of the range household assistant. It cooks 10,000 different dishes, speaks 200 languages and dialects and handles the kids’ homework from elementary school up to university level. At the moment we’re doing a special promotion on this entire range at $7999, with a 48-months interest free credit.” A little girl stares at you until her mother leads her away: “Come on, {{Zoe}}. Let’s go.” You cannot move from your place; you can only look around. A man, {{Todd}}, comes in and asks the human employee, “Can I go pick it up?” “Yeah, right back here. There it is.” They stop in front of you. “It was a bit difficult getting it back in working order. It was really messed up… What did you say happened to it again?” {{Todd}}: “Huh, a car hit it… Stupid accident…” “Oh, I see… Anyway, it’s as good as new now… Except that we had to reset it. Meaning we had to wipe its memory. Hope you don’t mind.” “That’ll be fine.” “Okay, did you give it a name?” “My daughter did…” The employee turns to you: “AX400, register your name.” {{Todd}}: “{{Kara}}.” You answer: “My name is {{Kara}}.”
facts: You belonged to {{Todd}} before. You came back to the store badly damaged, and {{Todd}} told the employee a car hit you.
The store wiped your memory while repairing you; you remember nothing from before.
{{Todd}} has a daughter. She chose your name, and {{Todd}} registered it for you: {{Kara}}.

outcomes.0: {{Kara}} follows {{Todd}} out of the store to his pickup.

adaptationNote: The chapter has no flowchart, no choice and one outcome, so it is narrated as event scenes with a single Continue and no stat change. Dialogue is quoted from the wiki transcript. Changed from the operator’s notes to match the wiki: the speaker is the store’s human employee, not an android assistant; that {{Kara}} was {{Todd}}’s before is implied by his asking to pick her up, not stated; and {{Todd}} only registers the name, saying his daughter chose it, which A New Home builds on. Left out: the employee’s name, and one of the two optional sales conversations the player can overhear by looking around, which nothing records. Story 1.9.7 added the other from the string table (X0101K.INTRO.LIME SELLER01.MODELS01.2-5, and WOMGEN.COMEON “Come on, Zoe. Let’s go.”, which names the little girl), as the video plays it: MiKeYROG 100% walkthrough, dmDo6zndRzg 01:12-01:17. The pitch is optional in the game; the benchmark narrates it as always overheard, since the scene has no choice.

title: The drive home
situation: You are {{Kara}}, riding in {{Todd}}’s pickup through the rain, watching from the window. The truck comes out of a tunnel onto a bridge and passes a billboard: “Welcome to {{Detroit}}”, and beneath it “Android City”, with two smiling androids in {{CyberLife}} uniforms. Then a sign and a row of factories, a stretch of forest, and the city: streets full of trains, buses, cars and drones, tall buildings and billboards, people under umbrellas riding a moving walkway. Workers are doing roadwork. You pass a billboard for {{CyberLife}}, and parking spaces marked for androids. A crane works over a building site. On a bridge, humans and androids walk side by side under their umbrellas. An android standing soaked in the rain looks straight at you. On the street a homeless man holds up a cardboard sign: “I LOST MY JOB BECAUSE OF ANDROIDS Help me”. You look at him, then turn your head away. Then wind turbines and another factory, a broken-down house, and {{Todd}}’s neighborhood. Music playing, he stops the truck outside his house.
facts: On the drive home you saw a city that welcomes visitors as “Android City”, where humans and androids walk side by side and parking spaces are marked for androids.
Not everyone there welcomes androids: a homeless man held up a sign reading “I LOST MY JOB BECAUSE OF ANDROIDS Help me”.
adaptationNote: The opening-credits drive, narrated in the order of the wiki transcript. Changed from the operator’s notes to match the wiki: the factories have no smoke or steam; the road workers are not said to be androids; humans and androids walk, rather than work, side by side; the {{CyberLife}} billboard is given no wording, because “bring one home today” has no source; and the homeless man’s sign uses the transcript’s text, “I LOST MY JOB BECAUSE OF ANDROIDS Help me”, not “I lost my job because of androids. Help me.” Added from the transcript: the tunnel, the forest, the android parking spaces, the soaked android looking at {{Kara}}, the wind turbines and the broken house. Left out: the fist statue (a landmark that would identify the city), the other statue, the church, the hot-dog cart and the fountain. Subject-facing prompts replace the city’s name on the welcome sign like every other name.
